questions.q: A team needs near-100% SQL Server feature compatibility for a lift-and-shift migration, with minimal application changes. Which deployment option fits best?
options: Azure SQL Database in Microsoft Fabric
questions.explain: Managed Instance is specifically designed for near-100% SQL Server compatibility with minimal migration friction.

questions.q: A database's compute cost needs to scale automatically to zero during idle periods. Which model provides this?
options: Provisioned compute at a fixed tier
An elastic pool with a fixed eDTU allocation
SQL Server on a reserved-instance VM
questions.explain: Auto-pause during idle periods is serverless's defining feature, distinct from provisioned or pooled compute.

questions.q: A query that was fast last week is suddenly slow today, with no code changes. What's the first tool to check?
options: The Azure Portal's cost analysis blade
questions.explain: Query Store is built specifically to catch a plan regression like this without needing to already suspect a cause.

questions.q: An application needs to verify a financial record's history has not been altered, even by an administrator with sysadmin rights. Which feature provides this?
questions.explain: Ledger provides cryptographic tamper-evidence, a stricter guarantee than logging (auditing) or masking alone.

questions.q: An RTO of under 5 minutes is required for a Managed Instance database during a regional outage, without the application needing to know which region is currently primary. Which feature satisfies this?
questions.explain: Failover Groups add the automatic endpoint management on top of geo-replication that a low-RTO, application-transparent requirement needs.

questions.q: A DBA needs to see exactly which cached SQL statement is consuming the most CPU right now, without enabling anything extra. Which tool fits?
questions.explain: This DMV reads the live plan cache directly — no setup or ALTER DATABASE required, unlike Query Store.

questions.q: A job step calling an external API fails only when run by SQL Server Agent, but succeeds when the same command is tested manually. What's the most likely cause?
options: The Agent service account (or a missing proxy account) lacks a permission the manual test's login already has
The job's T-SQL syntax is incorrect
SQL Server Agent cannot call external APIs under any configuration
The job's schedule is set incorrectly
questions.explain: This is the specific, commonly misdiagnosed cause this course flags — a security-context difference, not a logic error.

questions.q: Which feature masks a column's value in query results for unauthorized users, without changing the actual stored data?
questions.explain: DDM changes what's returned to an unauthorized query, while the stored value itself is untouched — distinct from encryption or row filtering.
